chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Quran will come on the Day of Resurrection in the best appearance/image, so it will pass by the Muslims and they will say, 'This man is from us.' It will pass them by to the Prophets, and they will say, 'He is from us.' It will pass them by to the Proximate Angels, and they will say, 'He is from us,' until it reaches the Lord of Might, Exalted and Majestic.

It will say, 'O Lord! So-and-so, son of so-and-so, I made his throat thirsty and I kept awake his night in the house of the world; and so-and-so, son of so-and-so, I did not make his throat thirsty and I did not keep awake his night.'
The Blessed and Exalted will say, 'Admit them into Paradise according to their stations.'
So it will stand up and they will follow it. It will say to the Believer, 'Recite and ascend.'
So he will recite and ascend until each man from them reaches his station which is for him, so it will make him descend into it.
ai.seo_question: How does the Quran intercede for believers on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of *Tajassum al-Qur'an* (personification of the Quran), where the text manifests as a living intercessor on the Day of Judgment. It highlights the Shia emphasis on the spiritual merit of *Mujahada* (struggle), specifically linking physical sacrifices like thirst and sleeplessness to elevated stations in Paradise. The narrative underscores the Quran's role not merely as a book, but as an active agent that guides believers to their divinely ordained levels through its own recitation.
